messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: App to evaluate R commands?
parts:
Greetings.  I'm just taking my first look at shiny.  I've looked at the examples, and they seem clear enough.  But I set myself the task of writing a simple command loop:

while(TRUE) {
    read a command from the user

    execute the command

    display the results
}

This is with all the latest software, installed on Friday, on Ubuntu 12.04.  I've appended the latest in a long series of iterations.  I think the gist of the problem is that I don't know how to get the R command input as a text string.

Thanks for any hints, help, etc., you can provide.

-- Mike

==== ui.R ====


library(shiny)

# Define UI for R-command application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

# Application title.
headerPanel("Run Some R Code"),

sidebarPanel(
textInput("userInput", "Input an R command:"),

submitButton("Run the command!")

),

mainPanel(
h4("Results:"),

verbatimTextOutput("result")
)
))

==== server,R ====

library(shiny)

# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

# Run the submitted command

inputCommand <- renderText({
input$userInput

})


output$result <- renderPrint({
nextCommand <- inputCommand
eval(parse(nextCommand()))
})

})

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: App to evaluate R commands?
parts:
You might want to take at look at rNotebook, an R package that allows you to run R in a browser.

http://ramnathv.github.io/rNotebook/

The online version is wired to OpenCPU instead of Shiny to partly overcome the security concerns that Joe pointed out. There are two modes: R mode and Rmd mode which can be used to run R code or knit an Rmd file.

The offline version is wired to Shiny, and can be run from your computer. There is still a security issue here, and you would need to have some firewalls in place.

This package is still under development and can be installed from its github repo.

Hope this is useful.

Cheers,
Ramnath
